headings.title: Discretionary leave to sue as poor person and counsel assignment
headings.reviewNote: Permits court in its discretion (except under subsection 3) to allow an indigent plaintiff to sue as a poor person without fees and to assign counsel, with costs recovered for court officers if plaintiff prevails.

headings.title: Minimum ten-dollar cost security for confined offenders
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits reducing security for costs below ten dollars in civil actions filed by confined state prison or correctional center offenders, unless no security for costs is required on filing.

headings.title: Cost waiver by certification for legal aid representation
headings.reviewNote: Permits waiver of costs without motion or court approval upon clerk-filed certification for parties represented by qualifying legal aid, law school clinics, or affiliated private counsel, with trial recertification and post-action review of guardian ad litem fees.

headings.title: Additional financial evidence and guardian ad litem fees
headings.reviewNote: Permits any party to present additional financial evidence and permits court to order a certifying party with present ability to pay a portion of guardian ad litem fees.

headings.title: Nonpayment of guardian ad litem fees not bar to future filings
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that failure to pay guardian ad litem fees shall not preclude future suits or motions to modify or limit the certifying party's prosecution or defense.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 5 subsections, statutory history, and 4 case annotations (Taylor, Scott, Coats, Francis); refined subsections 2, 3, and 4 titles to match exact statutory wording ('security for costs', permissive certification waiver, and additional financial evidence).

headings.title: Costs and fees for frivolous bad-faith proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Requires court after hearing to assess costs, reasonable expenses, attorney's fees, and party time compensation for frivolous and bad-faith claims, defenses, motions, or proceedings, while excluding liability for good-faith attorneys acting at client direction.

headings.title: Pre-1985 conduct and post-conviction review exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Excludes conduct occurring before September 28, 1985 and civil proceedings by a convicted person seeking judicial review of conviction.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and statutory history; tightened both titles to reflect conjunctive frivolous/bad-faith requirement, good-faith attorney protection, September 28, 1985 cutoff, and post-conviction review exception.
